content:
Rocco can now finally do web builds, which is achieved by Roc compiling to wasm and the engine supporting WebGPU. I have embedded an example on this post inspired by the classic PS1 game Kula World

https://pixelsprout.dev/devlog/rocco-on-the-web/
Neat! I got to level score 4250. The sound effects are nice!
This is just of teaser of what I am working on next... A full interactive tour of how to build a Rocco game, running in your browser (very much an early prototype)

pixelsprout said:

A full interactive tour of how to build a Rocco game, running in your browser (very much an early prototype)

What are you using to build the the interactive tour (including Roc beyond the game itself?

Steve Howell said:

I'm getting better at OrbWeaver:

Haha maybe I should add some more levels then :sweat_smile:

I'm not using anything too fancy, just Monaco for the editor and the plain old JavaScript and CSS for the rest. I'm also using the Roc interpreter inside the wasm bundle.

I had Claude do a little write-up of a particular piece of our codebase that uses Rocco directly. If you are considering building with Rocco, I think you will get a taste of what to expect. It has been fun for me! https://roc.lynrummy.com/rocco-emitters/
The article describes the dust devil shown below. A still image doesn't do it justice so see https://roc.lynrummy.com/safari-walk/. Let it warm up and then click D (for dust devil).
Thanks for the write-up. Happy to accept a PR for the extra fields to tune an emitter :blush:
GTA VI in Rocco in 2027 :smile:
Ah thanks will take a look. Don't worry about the failed tour build. I've got a fix.
@Steve Howell you're changes are good so I've merged. I think what I will do with emitters is move them into the node tree, this way they can attach to parent to groups and have a clear heirachy.

Sounds good! I've been trying to improve the safari movie today, and I'm getting to two areas that are always a bit of a struggle: pacing and focus. My protagonist is driving and then walking and then seeing things at the side of the road. It looks unnatural unless you get the acceleration just right or unless you properly focus on the barkoo as you approach the bar. Claude has the basic concepts down (smooth curves for acceleration of motion or focus-tightness) but the timing is hard to get. I haven't yet reached for a way that I can tune them myself through the UI. That might be an area where Rocco could help with some design work.
Yeah I think the UI package could gain some more components, such as sliders and check boxes. This would definitely help with fine tuning values.

See Safari Walk VI in Rocco today! https://roc.lynrummy.com/safari-walk/

Click W to get to the newly written scene from today (campfire). And then let it roll until you get to the bar. A few new tweaks are there along the way.

Safari Walk on Rocco v0.17.1 is deployed. It was straightforward. The changes revealed a slightly janky thing we were doing on our side with emitters that has since been cleaned up. https://roc.lynrummy.com/safari-walk/

(no new changes since the campfire that a couple folks looked at already)
